Relevant past experiences:
  1. The task is to trim overgrown rose bushes near the front porch, categorized as gardening. The child initially considered watering the plants or opening the shears but did not know the correct sequence of actions. The caregiver clarified the steps: put on gloves first, retrieve the pruning shears from the toolbench, then trim only the overgrown branches before closing the shears. The task succeeded as the child followed the guided steps to complete the pruning.

I walked to the washing machine and gently pulled its door open with my hands. Inside, I saw the damp socks. I reached in and grabbed them, making sure to hold them securely. Then I carried the socks to the clothes dryer. I stopped in front of the dryer and pulled its door open the same way as the washing machine. I dropped the damp socks inside the dryer. I didn’t close the dryer door or turn it on, as the task only asked to transfer the socks. I stood back to check my work—yes, the socks were safely in the dryer! 🎉

Great job, sweetie! You opened the washing machine just right, took out the damp socks, and put them safely into the dryer. I’m so proud of how carefully you followed each step—you’re really learning this well! 🌟
